intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the grand Joseon-era Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok rented from nearby shops. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry, and you can witness the ceremonial changing of the royal guard. Stroll through the palace grounds and visit the National Folk Museum inside the complex for deep cultural immersion.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most iconic traditional markets. Sample authentic Korean street food including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the vibrant, bustling atmosphere that has defined Seoul's food culture for over a century.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class & SM Entertainment District Tour
experiences.description: Take a professional K-Pop dance class at a Hongdae studio where trained instructors teach choreography from popular idol groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, and aespa. Afterward, explore the SMTOWN COEX Artium in Gangnam, a flagship K-Pop culture hub with exhibitions, merchandise, and live hologram performances celebrating Korea's global music phenomenon.

experiences.name: Insadong & Bukchon Hanok Village Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean wooden houses (hanok) with sweeping views of the city. Continue to the artsy Insadong district to browse galleries, traditional tea houses, and craft shops selling handmade ceramics, calligraphy, and Korean folk art. End with a cup of traditional omija tea at a historic teahouse.

experiences.name: Korean BBQ & Makgeolli Night in Mapo-gu
experiences.description: Experience an authentic Korean BBQ dinner at a local charcoal grill restaurant in the lively Mapo district, grilling samgyeopsal (pork belly) and galbi (beef short ribs) at your table. Pair the meal with traditional makgeolli (milky rice wine) and an array of banchan (side dishes). Finish the evening exploring the neon-lit streets of Hongdae for live busking performances and K-indie music culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 13:00. Take the AREX (Airport Railroad Express) to Hongik University Station or transfer to subway Line 3 toward Gyeongbokgung Station (approx. 70-90 min, ~₩4,150). Check in to Boutique Stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu and freshen up. Take a short orientation walk around the Gyeongbokgung neighborhood, exploring the surrounding hanok-lined alleys and getting your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Insadong Street (10-min walk from hotel) for your first taste of Seoul's cultural district. Browse traditional craft shops, street snacks, and art galleries. Grab a warm hotteok (sweet pancake) or bungeoppang (fish-shaped pastry) from street vendors for a cheap evening snack.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport snack)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick kimbap or ramyeon at a convenience store (GS25 or CU) near the airport or station (~₩2,000-4,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong Noodle Restaurant or a local gukbap (rice soup) spot near the hotel — try Cheonggyecheon-style bean paste stew for ~₩7,000-9,000

day_by_day.notes: Get a T-money card at the airport (₩4,000 deposit) and load ₩30,000 to start. This card works on all Seoul subways and buses. December is cold (0°C to -5°C), so dress in warm layers. Jetlag tip: stay awake until at least 9 PM local time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace first thing in the morning (literally steps from your hotel). Arrive early (opens 9:00 AM) to catch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 AM and 14:00 PM. Admission is ₩3,000. Wear hanbok rented nearby for FREE admission and a cultural photo experience (~₩15,000-20,000/hr for rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to explore Bukchon Hanok Village — a stunning neighborhood of preserved traditional Korean houses. Wander the narrow alleys, take photos, and soak in the atmosphere (free). Continue to Samcheong-dong Street for window shopping and café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square to see the illuminated statue of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin, beautifully lit in winter. End the evening at a nearby pojangmacha (street food tent) for tteokbokki and odeng (fish cake skewers).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby bakery — Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for bread and coffee (~₩3,000-5,000)
meals.lunch: Gyeongbokgung area jjigae restaurant — doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) set with rice and banchan (~₩8,000)
meals.dinner: Pojangmacha near Gwanghwamun — tteokbokki, odeng, and soondae (blood sausage) combo (~₩6,000-8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Since Day 2 is Wednesday, it will be open. The hanbok rental shops are clustered on the south and east gates. Bring hand warmers for the outdoor walking — December is bitterly cold in Seoul.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). Admission ₩3,000 for palace; Secret Garden guided tour ₩5,000 (book in advance or arrive early). The winter garden is hauntingly beautiful with bare trees and frost. This UNESCO World Heritage Site is a must.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace and Jongmyo Shrine (UNESCO site, ₩1,000). Jongmyo is the royal ancestral shrine of the Joseon Dynasty — one of the most serene and historically significant sites in Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun History & Culture Park (subway Line 2/4/5). Explore the futuristic Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — free to enter the outdoor areas and many indoor exhibitions. Browse the massive Dongdaemun shopping district, which comes alive at night with affordable fashion and street food.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — triangle kimbap + ramyeon cup (~₩3,500)
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village nearby — try a small Korean set meal (백반, baekban) for ~₩7,000-9,000
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun night market street food — dak-kkochi (grilled chicken skewers), hotteok, and tteokbokki (~₩5,000-7,000)

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours are conducted in Korean and English at set times — check the schedule at the gate. Jongmyo is closed on Tuesdays. Dongdaemun's shopping malls (Doota, Migliore) are open until 5 AM — great for late-night budget shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 1 to Jongno 3-ga and explore Tapgol Park (free) — Seoul's first modern public park with the 10-story marble Wongaksa Pagoda. Then walk through Pimatgol Alley, an ancient pedestrian lane with traditional Korean restaurants that have served locals for centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully restored urban stream running through central Seoul (free). Walk along the stream path from Gwanghwamun end toward Dongdaemun, passing colorful art installations and stone bridges. In winter, look for seasonal light festival decorations.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Namdaemun Market (Seoul's largest traditional market, open since 1414). Browse stalls selling everything from street food to clothing to kitchenware at rock-bottom prices. This is a great place to pick up budget souvenirs and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market (nearby) — kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) for ~₩6,000
meals.lunch: Pimatgol Alley restaurant — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set meal ~₩8,000
meals.dinner: Namdaemun Market — galchi jorim (braised hairtail fish) or kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) ~₩7,000-9,000

day_by_day.notes: Cheonggyecheon Stream is beautiful at night when lit up — consider returning after dinner for a romantic winter evening walk. Namdaemun Market is busiest in the evening. Keep your belongings secure in crowded market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park — take subway Line 3 to Gupabal Station, then bus to the park entrance (total ~1 hr from hotel). Hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail for stunning views of Seoul from ancient fortress walls. The winter scenery with snow-dusted peaks is spectacular. Entrance is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking or take a shorter loop trail back. The Daedongmun Gate section of the fortress wall offers excellent photo opportunities. Return to the city by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Hongdae (Hongik University) area on your way back — take Line 3 to Hongik University Station. Explore the vibrant street art, indie music scene, and youthful nightlife. Watch free busking performances on the main street.

meals.breakfast: Pack a convenience store breakfast before heading out — kimbap rolls and canned coffee (~₩3,000)
meals.lunch: Pack a hiking lunch — convenience store triangle kimbap, instant ramyeon at a mountain hut (~₩4,000-5,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food and restaurants — dukkbokki, Korean fried chicken (치킨), or a budget Korean BBQ (삼겹살) starting at ~₩10,000/person

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper hiking shoes and multiple layers — Bukhansan in December can have icy trails. Bring microspike traction devices if available. Sunset is around 5:15 PM in December, so plan your hike to be back at the trailhead by 4:30 PM. Bukhansan is extremely popular on weekends — arrive early (by 8:30 AM).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market — one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets (est. 1905). Famous for bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), and yukhoe (beef tartare). This is a legendary food destination and a cultural experience in itself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a trendy neighborhood of converted hanok houses turned into indie cafés, vintage shops, and small galleries. Very Instagram-worthy and free to explore. Pick up unique handmade goods at small boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Visit N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) via the free Namsan cable car (₩9,000 round trip) or hike up for free. The tower observation deck costs ₩16,000 but the outdoor deck and surrounding park are free. Attach a love lock to the famous fence and enjoy panoramic night views of Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market — mayak kimbap (5 pieces for ~₩3,000) and a bowl of kongnamul gukbap (~₩5,000)
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong hanok café — light Korean fusion meal or traditional sikhye (rice punch) and snacks (~₩8,000-10,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Street Food near Namsan — tteokbokki, corn dogs, grilled oysters (~₩8,000-10,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is best experienced in the morning when the food stalls are freshest and less crowded. Ikseon-dong is closed on Mondays for some shops. The hike up Namsan takes about 30-40 minutes and is a great way to save money on the cable car — but be cautious of icy paths in December.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Myeongdong — Seoul's most famous shopping and beauty district. Browse K-beauty stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young) for affordable skincare and cosmetics. Many stores offer free samples. Great for budget K-beauty shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to명동성당 (Myeongdong Cathedral) — a stunning Gothic-style Catholic cathedral (free to enter) that is one of Seoul's most beautiful landmarks. Then head to the nearby Sogong-dong underground arcade for budget shopping on clothing, accessories, and electronics.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Lotte Department Store basement food hall in Myeongdong for an affordable gourmet food experience — sample various Korean foods and pick up discounted ready-to-eat meals in the evening. Then head to nearby Euljiro for Seoul's coolest underground bar scene in converted print shops.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or nearby café — egg sandwich and Americano (~₩4,000-5,000)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food lunch — Korean corn dogs, tteokbokki, and hotteok (~₩7,000)
meals.dinner: Euljiro pojangmacha or old-school Korean restaurant — dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) or sundubu jjigae (~₩9,000)

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely touristy but the street food is genuinely good and cheap. Olive Young is the best budget K-beauty chain — look for their discount bins. Euljiro (을지로) is a must for experiencing Seoul's hipster-meets-industrial culture — bars and restaurants are hidden in alleyways between old printing factories.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 2 to Hongdae area and explore the Hongdae Free Market (check seasonal schedule — may be indoors in winter). Visit the Trick Eye Museum (~₩15,000) or the nearby Street Art Wall for free photo opportunities. Browse the many indie clothing and vintage shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Sinchon and Yonsei University campus — beautiful neo-Gothic architecture and a lively student district with extremely affordable food. Explore the campus and surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Han River (Hangang Park) at Yeouido — take subway Line 5 to Yeouido Station. Walk along the river and enjoy the winter night scenery. Visit the 63 Building observation area or just enjoy the riverside. Return via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae area bakery or convenience store (~₩3,000-4,000)
meals.lunch: Sinchon student restaurant — 학식 (university cafeteria) style meal or nearby 김밥천국 (Kimbap Cheonguk) for a full meal under ₩6,000
meals.dinner: Yeouido IFC Mall food court or nearby local restaurant — bibimbap or kimchi jjigae set (~₩8,000-9,000)

day_by_day.notes: Kimbap Cheonguk (김밥천국) is a legendary budget chain restaurant found all over Seoul — full meals for ₩4,000-7,000. Highly recommended for budget travelers. Han River in December is very cold — dress extremely warmly and bring hand warmers. Some riverside convenience stores remain open year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Deoksugung Palace (₩1,000) near City Hall — the only palace open on Mondays. Famous for its unique blend of Korean traditional and Western-style architecture. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the Daehanmun Gate (11:00 AM and 14:00 PM). Walk through Deoksugung Stone Wall Road (Doldam-gil), one of Seoul's most romantic walking paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Seoul Museum of History (free admission) near Gyeongbokgung — excellent exhibits on Seoul's transformation from ancient times to the modern metropolis. Then visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (free admission) — a lesser-known but beautiful palace with fewer crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Itaewon for a multicultural evening experience. Explore the diverse neighborhood, browse international restaurants, and visit Gyeongnidan-gil — a trendy street with boutique restaurants and bars. Great for experiencing Seoul's cosmopolitan side.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area — doenjang jjigae set at a local restaurant (~₩6,000-7,000)
meals.lunch: Near Deoksugung — packed city hall area has many affordable lunch spots; try a Korean lunch box (도시락) from a convenience store (~₩4,000-5,000)
meals.dinner: Itaewon — international food at budget prices; try Korean-Mexican fusion or a traditional Korean BBQ at a local spot (~₩10,000-12,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Deoksugung Stone Wall Road (Doldam-gil) is especially atmospheric in winter when lit with soft lights in the evening. The Seoul Museum of History is completely free and very well-curated — allow 1.5-2 hours. Itaewon has become less touristy in recent years and more authentically local.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (free admission) in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with over 220,000 artifacts spanning Korean history from prehistoric times to the Joseon Dynasty. Allow 2-3 hours. The museum grounds are beautiful even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon's Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (₩10,000) for world-class contemporary and traditional Korean art. Then walk through the nearby Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood — a hillside village with a bohemian atmosphere and great street art.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul! Head to Myeongdong Cathedral for the Christmas Eve Mass (free, but arrive early for seating) — an extraordinary cultural experience. Afterward, join the festive crowds in Myeongdong for Christmas street celebrations, light displays, and special seasonal food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — kimbap and warm soy milk (~₩3,500)
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria — affordable Korean set meals (~₩7,000-9,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal; Myeongdong area galbi (grilled beef ribs) restaurant or a Korean BBQ experience (~₩15,000-18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas is widely celebrated in South Korea (it's a public holiday on Dec 25). Seoul transforms into a winter wonderland with elaborate light displays throughout the city. Myeongdong Cathedral's Christmas Eve Mass is a beloved Seoul tradition. Book dinner reservations in advance if possible, as restaurants fill up quickly on Christmas Eve.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — Seoul's main Buddhist temple, located just a 10-minute walk from the hotel (free admission). On Christmas Day, experience the fascinating coexistence of Buddhism and Christianity in Korea. The temple's winter lanterns and decorations are beautiful. Attend morning prayers if you wish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Seochon (West Village) neighborhood — located west of Gyeongbokgung, this is a charming area of traditional hanok houses, indie bookshops, art galleries, and quiet cafés. Visit the studio of late artist Lee Sang-beom and the Tong-in Market for traditional Korean snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam (subway Line 2) for a different side of Seoul. Walk the famous Gangnam-daero boulevard, explore COEX Mall (free to browse), and visit the Bongeunsa Temple illuminated at night — a stunning contrast of ancient Buddhism against modern skyscrapers.

meals.breakfast: Seochon area traditional Korean breakfast — 해장국 (haejangguk, hangover soup) for a hearty winter meal (~₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Tong-in Market — use market tokens (₩5,000 for 5 tokens) to sample various traditional Korean dishes from different stalls
meals.dinner: Gangnam area — 순대국밥 (soondae gukbap) or 설렁탕 (seolleongtang, ox bone soup) at a local restaurant (~₩9,000-10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a national holiday in Korea — many shops and some restaurants may be closed or have reduced hours. Buddhist temples are always open. Tong-in Market's token system is a unique and fun budget way to try many different foods. Bongeunsa Temple in Gangnam is free to enter and magical at night.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — take subway Line 1 from Seoul Station to Suwon Station (about 1 hour, ~₩2,600). The fortress walls stretch 5.7 km around the city — walk the entire circuit for free (fortress entrance ₩1,000). Stunning winter views from the fortress towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market near the fortress and visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace (₩1,500). Return to Seoul by late afternoon. Stop at Seoul Station area to explore the Seoul Station Culture Station 284 (free) — a beautifully restored 1925 railway station turned cultural center.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your second-to-last evening at Dongdaemun Night Market — shop for last-minute gifts and souvenirs at bargain prices. The wholesale fashion district offers incredible deals on Korean fashion, accessories, and goods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or convenience store before departure (~₩3,000-4,000)
meals.lunch: Suwon local specialty — 수원 왕갈비 (Suwon Wang Galbi, large grilled beef ribs) — a must-try local dish (~₩12,000-15,000 for a budget portion)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — 24-hour kalguksu restaurant or ramen bar (~₩7,000-9,000)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon is very manageable as a day trip. The Hwaseong Fortress walk takes 2-3 hours at a leisurely pace. Suwon Wang Galbi is a famous local specialty — slightly more expensive but worth trying as a special meal. The Dongdaemun wholesale markets are best after 10 PM when they fill with buyers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — return to Gyeongbokgung area for any last-minute photos or visits you missed. Browse the Gyeongbokgung craft shops for final souvenir purchases — handmade hanji (Korean paper) goods, traditional tea, and ceramics make excellent budget gifts. Visit the nearby National Folk Museum of Korea (free with Gyeongbokgung ticket or separate free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Insadong for final souvenir shopping — Ssamziegil courtyard mall has unique handmade Korean crafts at reasonable prices. Pack your bags and check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or at the nearest subway station locker (₩2,000-4,000).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a classic Seoul restaurant. Then head to the airport via AREX from Seoul Station or Hongik University Station. Allow 90 minutes before your flight for travel and check-in.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — 해물순두부찌개 (seafood soft tofu stew) set at a local restaurant near the hotel (~₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong area — traditional Korean tea house with 식혜 (sikhye) and Korean rice cakes (~₩5,000-7,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell splurge — 삼겹살 (samgyeopsal, grilled pork belly) at a local BBQ restaurant near the hotel (~₩12,000-15,000 per person including side dishes)

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan airport transfer accordingly. AREX direct train from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport takes 43 minutes (₩9,500) or the all-stop train takes 66 minutes (₩4,150). You can do airport check-in at Seoul Station the day before (City Airport Terminal) to save time. Keep some cash for final transportation and airport expenses.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and take the AREX Express Train to Seoul Station (approx. 43 min, ~₩9,500). Transfer to Gyeongbokgung area by subway or taxi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. Freshen up and take a gentle orientation stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village (5–10 min walk from hotel) — admire the traditional hanok rooftops and narrow alleyways at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong Street for your first taste of Seoul's cultural heartbeat — browse art galleries, craft shops, and street snacks like hotteok (sweet pancakes) and tteokbokki.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Seoul Station food court or a convenience store kimbap set (₩3,000–5,000) while in transit
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung — a legendary ginseng chicken soup restaurant, perfect for warming up after travel (₩17,000–20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag may be a factor. Tosokchon often has queues; arrive before 18:00 to avoid the longest waits. Dress warmly as December in Seoul is cold (0–5°C).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) right from your doorstep — watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 and 14:00. Explore the grand palace grounds, Geunjeongjeon throne hall, and the beautiful Gyeonghoeru Pavilion (₩3,000 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the National Folk Museum of Korea located within the palace grounds (free with palace ticket). Then head to Gyeongbokgung's west side to explore Seochon Village (서촌) — a charming, less-touristy neighbourhood with indie cafés and art studios.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) illuminated at night, then head to Gwangjang Market (광장시장) for one of Seoul's most authentic street food experiences.

meals.breakfast: Café in Seochon or hotel vicinity — try a traditional Korean breakfast set with doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) and rice at a local sikdang (₩7,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Palace-area café or packed kimbap from a nearby convenience store eaten in the palace gardens
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap, and yukhoe (beef tartare) from market stalls (₩10,000–15,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — since today is Wednesday, it's open. Rent a hanbok (₩15,000–20,000/2hrs) near the palace for free entry and beautiful winter photos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) — book the Secret Garden tour in advance online (₩8,000 + ₩5,000 for garden). The winter-bare trees create a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace (창경궁) for a quieter, less-crowded royal experience (₩1,000 entry). Then visit the National Museum of Korean History in Gwanghwamun Square (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square to see the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin and King Sejong. Explore the underground Sejong Story exhibition (free). Enjoy the festive December lights around the square.

meals.breakfast: Juk (Korean rice porridge) at Bon Juk (본죽) near Anguk Station — nutritious and warming in winter (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.lunch: Dosirak (Korean lunchbox) café near Changdeokgung or a local noodle restaurant — try kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Cheongginaru (청기나루) or a similar traditional Korean restaurant near Gwanghwamun — try galbi-jjim (braised short ribs) or bibimbap (₩12,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours are limited — book at least 2–3 days ahead on the official palace website. Wear very warm layers; the garden tour is entirely outdoors for ~90 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (홍대) — Seoul's vibrant youth and K-culture district. Explore the street art, murals, and independent boutiques. Visit the Line Friends flagship store and the quirky KT&G Sangsangmadang arts complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area for more indie shopping and K-beauty stores. Visit the Ewha campus with its stunning ECC (Ewha Campus Complex) underground architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the Friday night live street performance scene near Hongik University Station Exit 9. Experience the busking culture that helped define K-pop's grassroots origins.

meals.breakfast: Hotel vicinity café or a Paris Baguette/Tous Les Jours bakery chain for a quick Korean-style pastry breakfast (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Hongdae's famous pork cutlet (돈까스) at Hongdae Haemul Pajeon or a trendy brunch café in the area (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Samgyeopsal (삼겹살) BBQ dinner at a Hongdae grill restaurant — cook your own pork belly at the table with soju or makgeolli (₩15,000–22,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Friday evening in Hongdae is lively and crowded — great energy for experiencing Seoul's youth culture. Keep an eye on your belongings in busy areas. Many shops open late (until 22:00–24:00).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower (남산타워) — take the cable car up (₩9,500 round trip) or hike the trail (30–40 min). Enjoy panoramic views of Seoul in winter clarity. See the famous love locks on the fence.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's premier shopping and street food district. Browse K-beauty flagship stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Sulwhasoo), fashion boutiques, and pick up Korean skincare products.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Myeongdong for the vibrant evening street food scene — try eomuk (fish cake skewers), tornado potato, Korean corn dogs, and hotteok. Visit명동 Cathedral (Myeongdong Cathedral) beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a local sikdang near your hotel — doenjang jjigae, rice, and banchan (₩8,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자) — famous for handmade kalguksu noodles and mandu dumplings, a Seoul institution (₩10,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food crawl for dinner — budget ₩10,000–15,000 for a variety of street snacks, or sit down at a nearby Korean BBQ spot

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Myeongdong is very busy. Go to N Seoul Tower in the morning for clearer skies and fewer crowds. The cable car may have queues on weekends — consider hiking up instead.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nami Island (남이섬) — take the ITX train from Cheongnyangni Station to Gapyeong Station (approx. 1 hr, ₩4,800), then shuttle bus + ferry to the island (₩16,000 round trip entry). Famous for its tree-lined paths and winter scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nami Island's walking trails, art installations, and peaceful riverside paths. The island is magical in December with frost and bare trees. Visit the Garden of Morning Calm (아침고요수목원) nearby if time permits (₩11,000 entry, shuttle available from Gapyeong).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul by early evening. Relax in your hotel area and explore Insadong's evening lantern-lit streets.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near hotel or convenience store onigiri and coffee before the train (₩4,000–6,000)
meals.lunch: Restaurant on Nami Island — try dak galbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) or bibimbap at one of the island's casual eateries (₩12,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong area — try a cozy Korean restaurant for sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) or doenjang jjigae set meal (₩10,000–14,000)

day_by_day.notes: Start early — aim for the 07:30–08:00 ITX train to maximize island time. Dress in your warmest layers; Nami Island is colder than central Seoul. The Garden of Morning Calm has a special winter light festival in December — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) in Yongsan — one of the largest museums in Asia with free permanent exhibitions covering Korean history from prehistoric times to the Joseon Dynasty. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the adjacent National Hangeul Museum (국립한글박물관) — free entry, fascinating exhibits on the Korean alphabet invented by King Sejong. Then explore Yongsan Electronics Market or the trendy Itaewon neighbourhood nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Itaewon (이태원) — Seoul's most internationally diverse neighbourhood. Browse Antique Furniture Street, Homo Hill's indie bars, and the vibrant restaurant scene representing cuisines from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café or bakery (₩6,000–9,000)
meals.lunch: Museum cafeteria or a nearby restaurant — try a Korean set lunch (정식) with multiple banchan side dishes (₩10,000–14,000)
meals.dinner: Itaewon — treat yourself to Korean-fusion cuisine or international food; try Plant Café for creative Korean dishes, or a local pojangmacha (street tent bar) for fried chicken and beer (chimaek) (₩15,000–22,000)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum is closed on Mondays — visit the Hangeul Museum first (open Mon) and plan the National Museum for another day if needed. Check official websites for holiday closures around Christmas.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을) in depth — walk the famous Bukchon 8 Views trail, peek into traditional craft workshops, and visit the Bukchon Traditional Culture Center for a hands-on experience (pottery or hanji paper craft, ~₩10,000–15,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Unhyeongung Palace (운현궁) — a smaller, intimate royal residence with fewer crowds, free entry. Then walk to Naksan Park (낙산공원) along the ancient Seoul City Wall for sweeping views over the city and Ihwa Mural Village below.
day_by_day.evening: Descend into Daehangno (대학로) — Seoul's theatre district. Check for evening performances of Korean musicals, nanta shows, or non-verbal performances (tickets ₩30,000–60,000). The area has a lively university-town atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a Bukchon area hanok café — barley tea, rice, and banchan (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Jongno area — try haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) and makgeolli at a traditional Korean restaurant (₩12,000–16,000)
meals.dinner: Daehangno — pre or post-show dinner at a local Korean restaurant; try budae jjigae (army stew) — a hearty, warming dish with a fascinating post-war history (₩12,000–15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Bukchon is a residential area — please be respectful of noise levels, especially in the early morning. The City Wall walk to Naksan is partially uphill but offers incredible views; wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) in Yongsan — a powerful and extensive museum covering Korean military history, with free entry to the main exhibitions and impressive outdoor exhibits including tanks and aircraft.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gangnam (강남) — take the subway to explore the famous district immortalized by Psy's song. Visit COEX Mall (코엑스몰) — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls — and the stunning COEX Starfield Library (free, Instagram-famous).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gangnam's Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong for a glimpse of Seoul's luxury lifestyle and K-pop entertainment company headquarters (SM Entertainment, YG nearby). Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or Anguk Station vicinity café (₩6,000–9,000)
meals.lunch: COEX food court or a restaurant in Gangnam — try a Korean BBQ lunch set or naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles, popular year-round) (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Apgujeong area — try a trendy Korean fusion restaurant or a classic galbi (grilled ribs) restaurant in Gangnam (₩20,000–28,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Norebang rooms typically cost ₩15,000–25,000 per person per hour — great fun in a group. COEX Starfield Library is free to visit but may be crowded on weekday evenings; go early if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in central Seoul near your hotel. Beautiful lanterns may still be displayed. Then explore the nearby Insa-dong Ssamziegil courtyard complex for artisan crafts and indie shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Museum of History (서울역사박물관) — free entry, excellent exhibits on Seoul's transformation from a Joseon-era capital to a modern metropolis. Walk through Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁) adjacent to the museum (free).
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration — head to Myeongdong Cathedral for the midnight mass atmosphere or festive carol concerts. Enjoy the city's Christmas lights and decorations around Cheonggyecheon Stream and City Hall Plaza.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas Eve breakfast treat — visit a popular Seoul café like Café Bora (카페 보라) near Gyeongbokgung for purple taro lattes and Korean pastries (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong area — traditional Korean restaurant for a jeongsik (full course Korean meal) with multiple banchan (₩12,000–18,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special dinner — try a nicer Korean restaurant in the Jongno area; enjoy a dakgalbi hotpot or a full Korean BBQ spread with colleagues or fellow travellers (₩20,000–30,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is very festive in Seoul — couples and friends gather in major areas. Expect larger crowds in Myeongdong and Hongdae. Book dinner reservations in advance if possible. City Hall's ice skating rink (if operating) is a fun festive activity.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea — many attractions remain open. Visit Deoksugung Palace (덕수궁) near City Hall — famous for its stone wall road (돌담길) and the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony. The adjacent Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) may have special exhibitions (free or low-cost entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Lotte World Tower in Songpa-gu — visit the observation deck (Seoul Sky, ₩29,000) for breathtaking 360° views of the city on a clear winter day. Explore Lotte World Mall and nearby Seokchon Lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Jongno/Insadong area for a relaxed Christmas evening. Visit a traditional Korean tea house (찻집) like Dawon inside Insadong for sikhye (sweet rice drink) and yaksik (sweet rice cake) — a peaceful, culturally rich end to Christmas Day.

meals.breakfast: Sleep in slightly and enjoy a leisurely brunch at a Gyeongbokgung-area café (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.lunch: Near Deoksugung — try ox bone soup (설렁탕) at a local restaurant, a warming and traditional Korean dish (₩10,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Jongno area — enjoy a Christmas dinner Korean-style with a hot pot (전골) meal shared at the table; try haemul jeongol (seafood hot pot) (₩15,000–20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Some smaller shops may be closed on Christmas Day, but major attractions, palaces, and restaurants are generally open. Seoul Sky observation deck can be booked online to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP, 동대문디자인플라자) — the futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed landmark. Explore the design museum, current exhibitions, and the surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park (free outdoor areas).
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse Dongdaemun Market — a massive fashion and fabric wholesale district. Even as a tourist, the scale and energy are fascinating. Visit Doota Mall or Hello apM for Korean fashion and accessories. Then head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a final peaceful walk along the waterway.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening out — head to Bukchon or Insadong for a K-culture farewell experience. Visit a traditional pojangmacha (street tent bar) for eomuk, tteokbokki, and makgeolli under the winter sky, or enjoy a Korean craft beer at a Jongno craft brewery.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or Anguk Station vicinity — try a Korean egg sandwich (계란 토스트) from a street cart, a beloved Korean comfort food (₩2,000–3,500)
meals.lunch: Dongdaemun area — try a famous local restaurant for ox tail soup (꼬리곰탕) or a hearty Korean stew (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong or Jongno — splurge slightly on a farewell Korean cuisine dinner; try a traditional hanjeongsik (한정식) multi-course Korean meal at a mid-range restaurant (₩25,000–40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dongdaemun is famous for staying open until 05:00 AM — if you're a night owl, the market comes alive after midnight. The DDP also hosts night markets and design events; check their schedule for December events.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — take one last walk through Gyeongbokgung area and the Bukchon alleyways you've come to love. Visit any remaining shops in Insadong for last-minute souvenirs: Korean tea, hanji goods, traditional ceramics, or K-beauty products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack up, check out of your boutique stay. Head to Incheon Airport via AREX Express Train from Seoul Station (allow 2–2.5 hours before departure including check-in and security). Browse duty-free shops at the airport for final Korean snack purchases (honey butter chips, Choco Pie, Korean ginseng).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport — carry the memories of 13 incredible days in Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast near the hotel — a warm bowl of haejang-guk (해장국, hangover/morning soup) or sundubu jjigae to fortify yourself for the journey (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Airport food court at Incheon — try one last Korean meal such as bibimbap or doenjang jjigae before your flight (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Incheon Airport is one of the world's best — arrive early to enjoy its cultural experience zones, traditional craft demonstrations, and excellent duty-free shopping. The AREX Express Train departs every 30 minutes from Seoul Station. Store luggage at the hotel until checkout if needed.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from ICN to boutique stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu (approx. 60–70 min by private car). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your hanok-style boutique accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around the immediate Gyeongbokgung neighborhood. Stroll along the iconic stone walls of Gyeongbokgung Palace exterior, explore the charming alleyways of Bukchon Hanok Village (a 10-minute walk), and admire the traditional tiled rooftops at dusk. Light jet-lag-friendly pace.
day_by_day.evening: Introductory dinner in Insadong, a 15-minute walk from the hotel — one of Seoul's most culturally rich dining districts. Visit a premium Korean fine-dining restaurant for a curated first taste of hansik (Korean cuisine).

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit; grab a light snack at the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Mingles (Michelin-starred modern Korean cuisine in Gangnam, or opt for nearby Jungsik Seoul) — alternatively, Bicena in Insadong for an elegant introduction to Korean royal court cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Prioritize rest after the long-haul flight. Ask hotel concierge to pre-book Day 2 Gyeongbokgung Palace guided tour tickets in advance. Bring warm layers — December in Seoul is cold (0°C to -5°C typical).

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace (literally steps from your hotel). Witness the ceremonial Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 AM. Explore the grand throne hall Geunjeongjeon, the serene Gyeonghoeru Pavilion, and the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds. Dress in rented hanbok for an immersive cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Bukchon Hanok Village for a deeper exploration — hire a private cultural guide to explain the history of the 600-year-old hanok houses. Continue to Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) for a guided tour of the secluded royal retreat.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong for premium Korean tea culture at a traditional tearoom (Suyeon Sanbang or O'Sulloc Tea House). Then enjoy dinner at a prestigious Korean barbecue restaurant featuring premium Hanwoo beef.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a traditional Korean morning spread (doenjang jjigae, rice, banchan) or Western option
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang near Gyeongbokgung — legendary ginseng chicken soup in a historic hanok setting, beloved by locals and royalty alike
meals.dinner: Hanwoo Club or Maple Tree House (Itaewon) — premium Hanwoo beef BBQ with tableside service and curated soju/makgeolli pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the Secret Garden tour (Changdeokgung Huwon) in advance — tickets are limited. Hanbok rental near the palace gates is available for approximately KRW 30,000–50,000/hour. Wear thermal layers under hanbok.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (the lesser-visited 'Palace of Serene Harmony') for a peaceful, crowd-free morning. Then explore the Seoul Museum of History adjacent to it for rich context on Seoul's 600-year history as a capital city. Private docent-led tour recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a bohemian neighborhood of independent galleries, artisan coffee shops, and traditional architecture. Visit the studio of local artists and browse curated Korean craft shops. Stop at Tongin Market for a traditional dosirak (lunchbox) experience using old brass coins.
day_by_day.evening: Evening visit to Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House) — the former presidential residence now open to the public, beautifully lit at night. Then dinner in the upscale Samcheong-dong area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Cafe Bora (Instagrammable purple taro latte and pastries in Bukchon)
meals.lunch: Tongin Market dosirak experience — select side dishes with brass coins for a fun, authentic, budget-friendly lunch amid a premium trip
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul (2 Michelin stars) — contemporary Korean cuisine with world-class presentation, located in Gangnam (20 min by private car)

day_by_day.notes: Cheong Wa Dae is free to enter but requires online reservation. Seochon is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. Samcheong-dong has excellent boutique wine bars for a post-dinner nightcap.

day_by_day.morning: Full immersion in K-culture: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan (30 min by private car) — one of Asia's largest museums. Explore ancient artifacts, Joseon Dynasty treasures, Buddhist art, and royal relics with a private English-speaking guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon and Haebangchon (HBC) — Seoul's most internationally diverse neighborhood. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art for world-class Korean and international contemporary art. Explore the high-end boutiques of Hannam-dong.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Itaewon's premium dining and cocktail scene. Visit a rooftop bar with Han River views for sunset cocktails, then dinner at one of Seoul's top restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Noryangjin Fish Market experience — take a private car to this iconic wholesale seafood market, select live seafood (king crab, abalone, sea urchin), and have it prepared fresh upstairs
meals.dinner: Gaon (3 Michelin stars) — the pinnacle of Korean fine dining, offering a meticulously crafted tasting menu rooted in royal court cuisine traditions

day_by_day.notes: Gaon requires reservations weeks in advance — ensure hotel concierge books this well ahead. Leeum Museum may have special winter exhibitions. Noryangjin Fish Market is most vibrant in the morning but accessible all day.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage site of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (1 hour south by private car). Walk the 5.7km fortress wall circuit with panoramic views of the city. Visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace within the fortress grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul. Explore Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the beating heart of Korean youth culture, street art, K-indie music, and creative fashion. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or explore street performances.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Seoul's legendary night food culture. Visit Gwangjang Market (a 20-min drive from hotel) for premium street food — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, and yukhoe (Korean beef tartare).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early start for Suwon day trip
meals.lunch: Traditional hanjeongsik (Korean full-course meal) in Suwon near Hwaseong Fortress — a multi-course spread of seasonal Korean dishes
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market premium street food experience followed by late-night pojangmacha (street tent bar) with makgeolli and pajeon (scallion pancakes)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is magical in winter — bring hand warmers. Saturday at Hongdae and Gwangjang Market will be busy and vibrant. Consider hiring a private food tour guide for the Gwangjang Market experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — Seoul's principal Buddhist temple, a 15-minute walk from the hotel. Participate in a premium temple stay morning program: meditate with monks, learn the art of Buddhist tea ceremony, and experience the tranquil temple grounds decorated with winter lanterns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic landmark. Visit the design exhibitions, fashion pop-ups, and the adjacent Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. Explore Dongdaemun Market for premium Korean textiles and fashion.
day_by_day.evening: Cheonggyecheon Stream evening walk — the beautifully illuminated urban stream running through central Seoul is especially magical in December with winter light festivals. End the evening with a premium dinner in the Jung-gu district.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel — early temple morning program
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang at Jogyesa Temple — Seoul's most celebrated temple food restaurant, offering exquisite Buddhist vegetarian cuisine (Michelin-recommended)
meals.dinner: Kwon Sooksoo or La Yeon (The Shilla Hotel, 2 Michelin stars) — refined Korean cuisine with panoramic city views

day_by_day.notes: Temple stay morning programs at Jogyesa require advance booking. La Yeon at The Shilla is one of Seoul's most prestigious dining experiences — reserve well ahead. Cheonggyecheon Stream is walkable from DDP.

day_by_day.morning: K-culture deep dive: Visit the SMTOWN COEX Artium in Gangnam — an immersive K-pop experience center featuring hologram performances, idol merchandise, and interactive exhibits. Then explore the iconic COEX Mall and its stunning Starfield Library.
day_by_day.afternoon: Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong luxury shopping district — Seoul's answer to Paris's Champs-Élysées. Browse flagship stores of Chanel, Dior, Bottega Veneta alongside Korean luxury brands like MCM and high-end Korean designer boutiques. Visit the Galleria Department Store's premium food hall.
day_by_day.evening: Gangnam nightlife experience — visit a premium karaoke norebang (private luxury room with full service), then cocktails at a rooftop bar in Gangnam.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul (InterContinental Seoul COEX) — French-Korean fusion by the legendary 3-Michelin-star chef
meals.dinner: Dosa (Gangnam) or Mosu Seoul (Michelin-starred, innovative Korean tasting menu) — cutting-edge contemporary Korean cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Cheongdam-dong is best explored in the afternoon when stores are fully open. Private luxury norebang rooms can be booked through the hotel concierge. December 21 is the winter solstice — the shortest day of the year.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nami Island (Namiseom) — a picturesque island 1.5 hours from Seoul by private car and ferry. Famous for its tree-lined avenues, the island is a beloved K-drama filming location (Winter Sonata). Explore the serene winter landscape, art installations, and riverside walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Petite France in Gapyeong — a whimsical French-themed cultural village and K-drama filming site. Explore the colorful buildings, Le Petit Prince exhibitions, and panoramic lake views. Return to Seoul by private car.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening back in Jongno-gu. Explore the atmospheric Pimatgol Alley — a historic narrow lane in Jongno with traditional Korean restaurants and pojangmacha stalls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early departure for day trip
meals.lunch: Nami Island restaurant — enjoy dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) or a riverside picnic-style spread, a regional specialty of the Chuncheon area
meals.dinner: Congdu (Jongno-gu) — elegant Korean fusion cuisine in a beautifully restored hanok building, walking distance from the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Nami Island ferry runs frequently. Private car is strongly recommended for this day trip for comfort and flexibility. Dress extremely warmly — lakeside winter temperatures can be biting.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive Korean cooking class experience — book a premium private class at a traditional hanok kitchen near Gyeongbokgung. Learn to prepare kimchi, bibimbap, japchae, and Korean royal court dishes under the guidance of a master chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Palace Museum of Korea (within Gyeongbokgung grounds) — a curated collection of royal artifacts, celadon ceramics, and Joseon Dynasty treasures. Then explore the Arario Museum in Insadong for contemporary Korean and international art.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Bukchon Hanok Village by night — the illuminated traditional houses create an ethereal atmosphere. End with a premium dinner at a restaurant known for seasonal winter Korean cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared in your morning cooking class — a true farm-to-table (or rather kitchen-to-table) premium experience
meals.dinner: Seorae Village (French district of Seoul) — dine at a premium French-Korean fusion restaurant for a cultural culinary crossover, or return to a top Korean establishment like Hansikgonggan

day_by_day.notes: Private cooking classes near Gyeongbokgung can be arranged through the hotel concierge. Book at least 3 days in advance. The National Palace Museum is free to enter and less crowded than the main palace.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower — take a private cable car up for sweeping panoramic winter views of the entire Seoul cityscape. Explore the observatory and the famous love lock installations. The tower is especially magical in December.
day_by_day.afternoon: Myeongdong luxury shopping and street food experience — Seoul's most famous shopping district buzzing with Christmas Eve energy. Visit flagship Korean beauty stores (Sulwhasoo flagship for premium K-beauty), department stores, and the vibrant street food stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve special experience — Seoul is festive and beautifully decorated in December. Attend a Christmas concert or performance at the Seoul Arts Center or Sejong Center for the Performing Arts. Then a lavish Christmas Eve dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja — legendary handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and dumplings, a Seoul institution since 1966
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve tasting menu at Gaon, Jungsik, or La Yeon — most top restaurants offer exclusive holiday menus; reserve weeks in advance

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Seoul is extremely lively — Myeongdong will be packed. Book holiday dinner reservations as far in advance as possible. Seoul is not a traditionally Christian city but Christmas is enthusiastically celebrated commercially and culturally.

day_by_day.morning: Peaceful Christmas morning walk along the Han River (Hangang Park) — rent a private bicycle or take a leisurely stroll along the frozen riverbanks. Visit Yeouido Hangang Park for beautiful winter scenery and views of the city skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Yeouido's IFC Mall and 63 Building — visit the 63 Art Gallery on the 60th floor for panoramic views. Then head to the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan for a moving and comprehensive history of the Korean War and Korean military history.
day_by_day.evening: Festive Christmas dinner followed by a luxury evening at a premium hotel bar. Visit the bar at The Shilla, Lotte Hotel Seoul, or Four Seasons Seoul for world-class cocktails and a glamorous Christmas atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast at hotel — request a premium spread or dine at the hotel's restaurant
meals.lunch: 63 Buffet at the 63 Building — panoramic views of Seoul with a premium international and Korean buffet spread
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at the Four Seasons Seoul's Boccalino or Charles H. bar — festive atmosphere with premium international cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Some attractions may have reduced hours on Christmas Day — verify in advance. The Han River is beautiful but very cold; dress in full winter gear. The War Memorial of Korea is closed on Mondays but open on Christmas Day (Friday).

day_by_day.morning: Premium wellness morning — book a private jimjilbang (Korean bathhouse) experience at a luxury spa facility such as Spa 1899 (Lotte Hotel) or Dragon Hill Spa. Experience the full Korean bathing ritual: hot tubs, cold plunge, exfoliation (Italy towel scrub), sauna rooms, and relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final deep-dive into K-culture: Visit the Korean Wave (Hallyu) exhibition or the K-Drama/K-Pop experience at the KOCCA (Korea Creative Content Agency) cultural centers. Explore the vibrant Mapo-gu area and Mangwon Market for authentic local neighborhood vibes.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner shopping in Insadong and Samcheong-dong — pick up premium Korean souvenirs: hanji (Korean paper goods), celadon ceramics, premium Korean teas, ginseng products, and artisan crafts. Final luxury farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market — a beloved local market less touristy than Gwangjang, with incredible tteokbokki, hotteok, and fresh produce stalls
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Mingles (Michelin 2-star) — Chef Kang Min-goo's masterful blend of Korean and global culinary techniques, one of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants

day_by_day.notes: Book luxury spa in advance — Dragon Hill Spa is open 24 hours. Insadong shops close around 9 PM. Pack purchased souvenirs carefully — celadon and hanji items are fragile. Confirm checkout time with hotel for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel. Take one final walk through Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds or along the palace wall if time permits. Check out of the boutique stay and arrange private luxury transfer to Incheon International Airport (allow 90 minutes for the journey plus buffer time).
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Explore the world-class ICN transit facilities — the airport features a Korean Cultural Street with traditional performances, a transit hotel spa, premium duty-free shopping (Korean ginseng, cosmetics, luxury brands), and excellent airport dining.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days immersed in Seoul's royal history, K-culture, world-class cuisine, and vibrant contemporary energy.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor a full Korean morning spread one last time: doenjang jjigae, grilled fish, rice, and assorted banchan
meals.lunch: Incheon Airport premium dining — visit the Korean restaurant on the transit level for a final bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) or bibimbap before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow minimum 3 hours before international departure at ICN. Private car transfer should be booked the night before — confirm with hotel concierge. Duty-free allowances vary by destination country; check limits for Korean ginseng and alcohol purchases. Keep all cultural souvenirs in carry-on if fragile.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX
